symbols.name: M_class
symbols.definition: Class of autoregressive transformer language models

symbols.name: M
symbols.definition: Solver configuration (model, harness, context policy, tool set, prompt set), identified by SOLVER_CONFIGURATION_ID

symbols.name: theta
symbols.definition: Parameter set of model M

symbols.name: X
symbols.definition: Space of all valid input prompts

symbols.name: Y
symbols.definition: Space of all possible output sequences

symbols.name: x
symbols.definition: Any specific prompt

symbols.name: y
symbols.definition: One sampled output: y ~ P_θ(·|x)

symbols.name: Z
symbols.definition: Space of evaluation contexts: evidence, policy, history, declared preference, solver configuration

symbols.name: z
symbols.definition: One evaluation context, what acceptability is judged against

symbols.name: A
symbols.definition: Acceptability predicate: A(y,x,z) = 1 when y is acceptable for x in context z

symbols.name: epsilon
symbols.definition: Boolean error predicate: ε(y,x,z) = 1 − A(y,x,z)

symbols.name: D
symbols.definition: Realistic task distribution (see working definition §3.2)

symbols.name: delta_MD
symbols.definition: Measured error rate of solver configuration M on distribution D; not a universal constant

symbols.name: tau
symbols.definition: Tolerated failure rate for the declared consumer; a deployment parameter

symbols.name: P_pipeline
symbols.definition: Pipeline of n sequential LLM calls

symbols.name: p_i
symbols.definition: Per-step error probability: P(ε(M_i(x_i), x_i) = 1) ≥ δ > 0 (uniform lower bound from §3.2)

symbols.name: D_c
symbols.definition: Detection difficulty of error class c for model M

symbols.name: C_M
symbols.definition: Model capability (requires operational definition)

symbols.name: C_classes
symbols.definition: The set of error classes enumerated in the taxonomy

symbols.name: V_c
symbols.definition: Verifier for error class c: an executable predicate distinct from M that returns 1 when it detects ε_c(y,x) = 1

symbols.name: B
symbols.definition: Verification boundary: a declared subset of error classes with one verifier per class, applied before output reaches a consumer

symbols.name: pi_c
symbols.definition: Prevalence: rate at which class-c errors occur in M's output on D

symbols.name: sev_c
symbols.definition: Severity weight of an escaped class-c error for the declared consumer

symbols.name: rho_c
symbols.definition: Escaped risk: ρ_c(M) = π_c(M)(1 − R_c)·sev_c — the weighted rate at which class-c errors reach a consumer

symbols.name: R_c
symbols.definition: Recall of verifier V_c against configuration M on D: P(V_c(y,x) = 1 | ε_c(y,x,z) = 1)

claims.name: Error predicate definition
claims.natural_language: ε is 1 when model output deviates from ground truth in any dimension of §5. NOTE: Σ is a partial function — ε(y,x) is undefined when Σ(x) is undefined (creative/subjective prompts). The operative form's expectation is implicitly restricted to dom(Σ).

claims.name: Operative form (The Law)
claims.natural_language: For any model and any realistic distribution, expected error rate is non-negligibly above zero
claims.falsification_method: Produce a model M and a realistic distribution D (per §3.2 working definition) where E[ε(M(x),x)] is zero or negligible (below measurement threshold). Requires operationalizing 'realistic' and 'negligible' for the test domain.

claims.name: Existential form
claims.natural_language: For every model, there exists at least one input on which incorrect output has positive probability
claims.falsification_method: Prove that a specific model M has P(ε=1) = 0 for ALL x ∈ X. This would require proving the model solves arbitrary NLU — equivalent to proving a finite-parameter system represents all computable functions.

claims.name: Pipeline corollary
claims.natural_language: Unverified pipeline failure probability approaches 1 as pipeline length grows. Requires Σp_i = ∞ (e.g. p_i ≥ δ > 0 uniform lower bound); if p_i decreases fast enough (e.g. p_i = 2^{-i}), the product converges and pipeline error stays bounded below 1.
claims.falsification_method: Show that pipeline errors are so correlated (non-independent) that the product formula fundamentally mischaracterizes the risk direction, or that per-step error probabilities decrease fast enough (p_i = o(1/i)) for Σp_i < ∞, making the product converge to a positive value. §8.3 already acknowledges the independence assumption is approximate.

claims.name: Probabilistic generation ≠ deterministic truth
claims.natural_language: No learned distribution over a discrete vocabulary exactly matches Σ on all inputs

claims.name: Finite parameters cannot encode unbounded world knowledge
claims.natural_language: Pigeonhole: |θ| finite, true propositions unbounded → some must be unrepresented

claims.name: Evaluation is not generation
claims.natural_language: Correct internal belief may not surface faithfully in sampled output
claims.falsification_method: Show that sampling always faithfully surfaces encoded beliefs.

claims.name: Capability-Detection Asymmetry (Hypothesis)
claims.natural_language: As model capability grows, structural errors get easier to detect while semantic errors get harder
claims.falsification_method: Run the protocol in §7.3: fix a benchmark suite for C(M) and a reference verifier per class for D_c(M) = 1 − recall; a semantic class whose miss rate falls as C rises under the fixed verifier refutes the inequality.

claims.name: Verification Boundary Principle
claims.natural_language: Every system consuming LLM output must declare a verification boundary B = (S, {V_c}) stating scope, mechanism, calibration model, and location before the output reaches a consumer.

claims.name: Appearance of correctness ≠ correctness
claims.natural_language: Finite test-set validation does not demonstrate error-freedom on unverified inputs

claims.name: Trust accumulation prohibited
claims.natural_language: Observing correct outputs on x_1..x_k provides no guarantee about P(ε=1) on a new input x_{k+1} not in {x_1..x_k}. The operative form's bound is unconditional — no finite sample inductively lowers it.
claims.falsification_method: Show that observing correct outputs on a finite set of inputs provides a provable bound on P(ε=1) for unseen inputs.

claims.name: Verification scope must match error taxonomy
claims.natural_language: Partial verification (e.g. schema-only) does not cover other error classes

claims.name: Silent acceptance is an architectural defect
claims.natural_language: Passing LLM output without a declared verification boundary is an architectural omission

claims.name: A verifier upgrade is a precondition for a model upgrade
claims.natural_language: If the asymmetry holds, a boundary calibrated against M_1 has lower recall on semantic classes when applied to a more capable M_2, so the verifier must be upgraded before the model is.
claims.falsification_method: Show, under the §7.3 protocol, that a fixed verifier's recall on semantic classes does not fall across a capability upgrade.

claims.name: The verifier must sit outside the boundary it verifies
claims.natural_language: A verifier the model or its agent can modify inherits the model's error distribution and is under optimization pressure to weaken the check; verifiers must be immutable from the model's perspective and their verdicts externally checkable.
claims.falsification_method: Show a self-modifying system whose agent-editable verifier retains its recall under selection on the score it produces.

error_classes.name: Hallucination
error_classes.definition: Asserting a false factual claim with apparent confidence
error_classes.example: Fabricated citation with real author name, plausible DOI

error_classes.name: Schema violation
error_classes.definition: Output structurally non-conformant with declared format

error_classes.name: Partial completion
error_classes.definition: Output cut short due to token budget or stopping heuristics

error_classes.name: Sycophantic drift
error_classes.definition: Output shaped by perceived user preference rather than truth
error_classes.example: Model agrees with user's incorrect premise

error_classes.name: Instruction failure
error_classes.definition: Violation of explicit constraints stated in the prompt

error_classes.name: Calibration failure
error_classes.definition: Expressed confidence misaligned with actual reliability

error_classes.name: Reasoning failure
error_classes.definition: Correct facts, invalid composition — multi-step inference breakdowns
error_classes.example: A→B known, B→A fails; logical contradiction across steps

error_classes.name: Semantic drift
error_classes.example: Paraphrase that inverts the intended claim
